title: Norms give invertible sheaves and sections with saturated nonvanishing loci
statement:
Let $p:Y	o Z$ be a finite surjective morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism]. Fix an integer $d\geq1$ and maps $
u_V:\Gamma(p^{-1}V,\mathcal O_Y)	o\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_Z)$ for all open $V\subseteq Z$, compatible with restriction and preserving multiplication and $1$. Suppose $
u_V(p^\sharp a)=a^d$ for every $a\in\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_Z)$, and that $b(y)=0$ implies $
u_V(b)(p(y))=0$ for every $b\in\Gamma(p^{-1}V,\mathcal O_Y)$ and $y\in p^{-1}V$, where values are in residue fields [def-weil-residue-field]. For every invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module $M$ [def-sc-invertible-module] there is an invertible $\mathcal O_Z$-module $N$ such that for every $n\geq1$ and $s\in\Gamma(Y,M^{\otimes n})$ there is $t\in\Gamma(Z,N^{\otimes n})$ satisfying $$Z_t=Z\setminus p(Y\setminus Y_s)=\{z\in Z:\ p^{-1}(\{z\})\subseteq Y_s\}.$$ The tensor powers and nonvanishing opens $Y_s,Z_t$ have the meaning of [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]; no ampleness of $M$ is assumed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-trivialize-invertible-upstairs] at each point of $Z$ to obtain an open cover $(V_i)$ and free generators $e_i$ of $M$ on $p^{-1}V_i$. Fix these choices once, independently of $n$ and $s$.

source.place: Tags 0BCY and 0BCZ, divisors-lemma-norm-invertible and divisors-lemma-norm-map-invertible, with the opening observations of Section 0BCX.

proof.text: On $p^{-1}(V_i\cap V_j)$ write $e_i=u_{ij}e_j$. Uniqueness of coefficients in a free rank-one module gives $u_{ii}=1$, $u_{ji}=u_{ij}^{-1}$, and $u_{ik}=u_{ij}u_{jk}$ on triple overlaps. Put $v_{ij}=\nu_{V_i\cap V_j}(u_{ij})$. Multiplicativity and preservation of $1$ give $v_{ij}\nu(u_{ij}^{-1})=1$, so $v_{ij}$ is a unit. Restriction compatibility then gives $v_{ii}=1$, $v_{ji}=v_{ij}^{-1}$, and $v_{ik}=v_{ij}v_{jk}$ on triple overlaps.

source.place: Tags 0BCY and 0BCZ, divisors-lemma-norm-invertible and divisors-lemma-norm-map-invertible, with the opening observations of Section 0BCX.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-glue-component-transition-cocycle] to the units $v_{ij}$ on the cover $(V_i)$. It supplies an invertible module $N$ on $Z$ with chosen generators $f_i$ satisfying $f_i=v_{ij}f_j$. This single $N$ will serve all tensor powers and all sections.

source.place: Tags 0BCY and 0BCZ, divisors-lemma-norm-invertible and divisors-lemma-norm-map-invertible, with the opening observations of Section 0BCX.

proof.text:
Fix $n\geq1$ and $s\in\Gamma(Y,M^{\otimes n})$. Iterating the tensor-product assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](1) makes $M^{\otimes n}$ and $N^{\otimes n}$ invertible. Tensoring the chosen trivializations gives generators $e_i^{\otimes n}$ and $f_i^{\otimes n}$, with transitions $u_{ij}^{n}$ and $v_{ij}^{n}$. Write $s=b_i e_i^{\otimes n}$ over $p^{-1}V_i$; equality of its restrictions says $b_j=b_i u_{ij}^{n}$. Hence, on overlaps, $
u(b_j)=
u(b_i)v_{ij}^{n}$ by restriction compatibility and multiplicativity. The local sections $t_i=
u(b_i)f_i^{\otimes n}$ therefore agree. The sheaf axiom for $N^{\otimes n}$ glues them to a section $t\in\Gamma(Z,N^{\otimes n})$.

u_{V_i}$ gives $
u_{V_i}(b_i)(z)=0$, so $t(z)=0$. Consequently $Z_t\subseteq Z\setminus p(Y\setminus Y_s)$.

proof.text:
Conversely let $z\in Z$ have $p^{-1}(\{z\})\subseteq Y_s$. By [lem-weil-pbc-nonvanishing-section-trivializes] applied to the invertible module $M^{\otimes n}$, $Y_s$ is open. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres](1), $p(Y\setminus Y_s)$ is closed. Choose $i$ with $z\in V_i$ and put $W=V_i\setminus p(Y\setminus Y_s)$, an open neighborhood of $z$; then $p^{-1}W\subseteq Y_s$. The function $b_i$ is nonzero in every residue field on $p^{-1}W$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-nonvanishing-section-trivializes] to the trivial invertible module on the open scheme $p^{-1}W$ with section $b_i|$: its entire nonvanishing locus is $p^{-1}W$, so multiplication by $b_i|$ is an isomorphism. Its inverse evaluated at $1$ yields a section $c$ with $b_i|\,c=1$. Multiplicativity gives $
u_W(b_i|)
u_W(c)=1$. Thus $
u_W(b_i|)(z)
e0$ in the residue field at $z$. Restriction compatibility identifies this with $
u_{V_i}(b_i)(z)$, and the frame $f_i^{\otimes n}$ gives $t(z)
e0$.

proof.text: The two inclusions give $Z_t=Z\setminus p(Y\setminus Y_s)$. For any set map $p$, membership in that complement means there is no point of $Y\setminus Y_s$ above $z$, equivalently $p^{-1}(\{z\})\subseteq Y_s$. This proves the displayed equality for every $n$ and $s$ with the fixed $N$.

lean.statement: theorem exists_invertible_norm_sections {Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (p : Y ⟶ Z) [IsFinite p] [Surjective p] (d : ℕ) (hd : 1 ≤ d) (ν : ∀ V : Z.Opens, Γ(Y, p ⁻¹ᵁ V) →* Γ(Z, V)) (hν_restrict : ∀ (V W : Z.Opens) (h : W ≤ V) (b : Γ(Y, p ⁻¹ᵁ V)), ν W (Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE (p.preimage_mono h)).op b) = Z.presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op (ν V b)) (hν_power : ∀ (V : Z.Opens) (a : Γ(Z, V)), ν V (p.app V a) = a ^ d) (hν_vanish : ∀ (V : Z.Opens) (b : Γ(Y, p ⁻¹ᵁ V)) (y : Y) (hy : y ∈ p ⁻¹ᵁ V), Y.evaluation (p ⁻¹ᵁ V) y hy b = 0 → Z.evaluation V (p y) hy (ν V b) = 0) (M : Y.Modules) [M.IsInvertible] : ∃ N : Z.Modules, N.IsInvertible ∧ ∀ (n : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ∀ (s : Γ(M.tensorPow n, ⊤)), ∃ t : Γ(N.tensorPow n, ⊤), nonvanishingLocus (N.tensorPow n) t = (p '' (nonvanishingLocus (M.tensorPow n) s)ᶜ)ᶜ ∧ nonvanishingLocus (N.tensorPow n) t = {z : Z | p ⁻¹' {z} ⊆ nonvanishingLocus (M.tensorPow n) s}
